description: An ESP8266 development board with an ESP-12E module, a CP2102 USB-serial chip and a 3.3 V regulator, with two active-low LEDs.
summary: The board runs the user's sketch in the iynk interpreter. Pins, PWM, I2C, serial and timing follow the nodemcu board profile. It is not the ESP8266 chip.
led: On-board LED, active low: LOW turns it on.

models.1: Arduino-C++ subset run by the interpreter with the NodeMCU pin map, where D4 is GPIO2.
models.2: Digital I/O on D0 to D8, TX, RX, SD2 and SD3, PWM on every GPIO, interrupts on every GPIO except GPIO16 (D0).
models.3: 10-bit analog read on A0 through the board divider, I2C master on D2 and D1, serial output, and the two active-low LEDs on GPIO2 and GPIO16.

not.1: The Xtensa L106 core, the Wi-Fi stack and flash behaviour. The request stub for web-server lessons is not a radio.
not.2: The boot-mode pins GPIO0, GPIO2 and GPIO15.
not.3: The CP2102 bridge and the 3.3 V regulator limits.

gap: The on-board LEDs are active low: digitalWrite(LED_BUILTIN, LOW) turns them on. D-numbers are not GPIO numbers: D4 is GPIO2. A0 reads 0 to 3.3 V through a divider, and GPIO16 has no interrupt. No electrical ratings are listed yet, so no pin-overload check exists for this board.
